newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy takes action in Adriatic to deter Albanians.
newsitem.headline: Italy takes action in Adriatic to deter Albanians.

text.p: Italy acted on Monday to stem an exodus from Albania, saying its shores had become a haven for illegal immigrants using the country's chaos as an opportunity to leave for a better life abroad.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi said after talks with Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino that they had reached agreement to conduct naval patrols in the Adriatic to halt the flow, which rose on Monday to close to 12,000 people since March 13.

Italy had also responded positively to an Albanian appeal for emergency food and medical aid to be sent to the country, where order has broken down in wide areas of the south after an armed revolt erupted this month, Prodi said.
"There will be an agreement between Italy and Albania to patrol the Adriatic in order to halt the flow of refugees completely," Prodi told a news conference.
"Patrols also means controlling the coasts," he said.

He did not make clear whether Italian ships would enter Albanian territorial waters, though military sources said the Navy was already carrying out orders to intercept Albanian boats and advise them to turn back for home.
"We must make sure that the Italian Navy...stops illegal immigration and stops it in Albanian waters before they leave," Defence Ministry under-secretary Massimo Brutti told Italian television.

The operation follows mounting evidence that recent arrivals were no longer genuine refugees but illegal immigrants looking for a better life who had paid Albanian mafias money for a passage, Italian officials said.
"The people reaching our shores (are) men and women from areas which have not even been touched by the revolt," Interior Ministry under-secretary Giannicola Sinisi said.

"They are looking for a better life, better-paid work. In short, they are immigrants," he said. "I can understand it but we cannot accept them. The law says they should be turned away at the border or repatriated."
Fino, who heads a national unity government installed in response to armed anarchy in the impoverished Balkan state, said he wanted Albanians to remain and help rebuild the country.
"We agree that Italy should patrol the entire Adriatic to stop this exodus because Albania's problems have to be resolved by the Albanians themselves in Albania," Fino said.
He said international relief aid was a crucial element in any attempt to stem the exodus. "That is the only way to give Albanians faith in this government's ability to govern," he said.
European Union foreign ministers, meeting in Brussels on Monday, again shied away from organising a multinational military force to help restore order in the former communist state.

But the ministers said they would not object to individual countries sending troops to act as security escorts for humanitarian aid convoys. They announced the despatch of a new advisory mission to Albania, the second in as many weeks.
Fino was to meet the EU ministers on Tuesday when they gather in Rome.
Italian television said Italy, France, Spain and Portugal were expected to provide forces to any security operation, with Greece, Romania and Hungary contributing at a later stage.
